title: Miguel de Navascués - CV
text:
I am a researcher at the CBGP (Centre de Biologie pour la Gestion des Populations - INRAE) in Montpellier. My work focuses on the development and evaluation of statistical methods for analyzing population genetic data to infer evolutionary processes, including genetic drift, gene flow, and selection. Currently, my research is centered on three lines:

Simulation-based methods for the joint inference of demographic and adaptive processes.
Analysis of temporal population genetic data, such as data from monitored or experimental populations.
Integrative demographic inference combining genetic and demographic data (such as capture-recapture data).

title: GDR-AIEM : annual meeting 2025
text: Last 5 to 7 November 2025 there was the Annual Meeting of the GDR-AIEM in Saint-Martin-de-Londres (France). Two people from our group at CBGP presented their work. Paul Bunel, presented his work on the use of Hidden Markov Models for the inference of effective population size and selection coefficient of loci under selection from temporal series of genetic data (Uhl et al. 2025). Jules Romieu presented his work using simulation-based inference for characterizing the proportion of the genome that is affected by adaptive introgression.

title: Webinar about Peer Community In
text: Last 13 january 2026 there was a Webinar organised by INRAE’s ECODIV division about Peer Community In (PCI) and Peer Community Journal (PCJ). There were several presentations, and among them I presented PCI Evolutionary Biology. The whole seminar (2h, in French) is available in YouTube.

title: Miguel de Navascués — Population Genetics
text:
I am a researcher at the CBGP (Centre de Biologie pour la Gestion des Populations - INRAE) in Montpellier. My work focuses on the development and evaluation of statistical methods for analyzing population genetic data to infer evolutionary processes, including genetic drift, gene flow, and selection. Currently, my research is centered on three lines:

Simulation-based methods for the joint inference of demographic and adaptive processes.
Analysis of temporal population genetic data, such as data from monitored or experimental populations.
Integrative demographic inference combining genetic and demographic data (such as capture-recapture data).
